title: Berry Overnight Oats
subtitle: Oats soaked with yoghurt and topped with mixed berries
excerpt: Rolled oats soaked overnight in milk and yoghurt soften into something creamy and ready to eat without any cooking. Fresh blueberries and strawberries piled on top in the morning make it feel like more of a breakfast than a bowl of cereal. The vanilla is not optional, it lifts the whole thing.
sourceNotes: A variation on the overnight oat method, popularised in the UK and US through meal-prep culture. Berry toppings are a summer staple when fresh British berries are at their best, strawberries from June, blueberries through July and August.

recipe.batchNotes: Make up to 4 portions in individual jars. Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days. Add the berries on the morning of serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepared the night before. Top with berries in the morning only.

content.text: Overnight oats let you do breakfast the night before. Rolled oats soaked in milk and yoghurt swell and soften while you sleep, turning into something thick and creamy that needs no cooking and no morning effort beyond opening the fridge. The berry topping, {{blueberries}} blueberries and {{strawberries}} strawberries, goes on fresh in the morning. You get cold, soft oats with fruit that still has some bite. The {{vanilla-extract}} vanilla extract stirred into the base makes a real difference. Without it the oats taste a little flat.

Measure the {{rolled-oats}} rolled oats into a medium bowl or two individual jars. Pour over the {{whole-milk}} milk, add the {{greek-yoghurt}} Greek yoghurt, {{honey}} honey, and {{vanilla-extract}} vanilla extract. Stir until everything is combined and the honey is dissolved into the liquid rather than sitting in a pool at the bottom.

Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, overnight is ideal. The oats will absorb the liquid and swell considerably. In the morning, stir the oats and check the consistency. If they're very thick, loosen with a tablespoon or two of extra milk. Hull and halve the {{strawberries}} strawberries and pile them over the top with the {{blueberries}} blueberries. Eat straight from the fridge.
Scatter a tablespoon of granola over the top just before eating for a bit of crunch.
In autumn, swap the summer berries for sliced apple and a pinch of cinnamon stirred through the base.
Use oat milk or almond milk in place of whole milk for a dairy-free version, the texture is slightly thinner but still works well.
A few blackberries stirred through instead of left on top bleed colour into the oats and turn the whole bowl a deep purple, which children tend to find interesting.

Oats still feel chewy after 8 hours: the fridge temperature may be very cold, which slows the softening. Leave them 10 hours next time, or let them sit at room temperature for 10 minutes before eating.
Mixture too runny: different yoghurt brands vary enormously in thickness. Next time, use a thicker Greek yoghurt or reduce the milk by 20 ml.
Berries added the night before: strawberries in particular release a lot of juice and make the base watery. Always add the fruit in the morning.
